text:
Dylan Guenther is back, and Utah is winning again. He and Clayton Keller returned to the lineup in Winnipeg on Nov. 23 after both had been out since early in the month, and after a quiet first night (CBS Sports called it a tough one) the Mammoth beat Minnesota and then Nashville 6-5 on Friday. Guenther had a goal and an assist against the Wild and the assist on Friday.

His season line (15 points in 21 games) is a bit light for a player Evolving-Hockey rated 53rd among forwards last season, and it leans hard on the power play: 10 of his 15 points. His shooting is normal (13% against a 13 to 17% expected range), so the gap is at five on five, where Utah has scored 3.5 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice.

The scoring instinct is still there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 92nd percentile for chances from the home-plate area last season. Watch his minutes: 20.7 on Friday, up from around 17.
